set.body:
Objective:
Implement Frame physical data as scoped sequences of Arrow-compatible record batches on JVM and Scala.js without exposing JVM-only memory types in shared APIs or inventing a competing general storage format.

Required model:
- Separate logical DType, field nullability, physical encoding, and buffer layout.
- Primitive nulls use validity bitmaps; placeholder values in invalid slots have no meaning.
- Shared Buffer and ArrayData contracts are platform-neutral. JVM ArrowBuf or optional FFM access and JavaScript ArrayBuffer or typed-array access live behind platform modules.
- Materialized batches and tables have explicit owned or borrowed lifetimes. Lazy plans do not own open streams.
- Slicing may share buffers; mutation is confined to builders that cannot unsafely alias finished values.

Initial types:
Boolean, Int32, an explicit cross-platform Int64 policy, Float32, Float64, UTF-8, timestamps, and dictionary encoding. Nested list and struct layouts may remain follow-on work if the first contracts leave a lawful extension seam.

Acceptance:
- RecordBatch and scoped batch-source contracts preserve schema and chunk boundaries.
- Required and nullable primitive arrays pass Arrow-layout fixtures, slicing laws, and scalar/vector access parity on JVM and JS.
- No primitive column stores boxed Option or Any values.
- Ownership tests cover retained slices, borrowed inputs, deterministic close, leak accounting where available, and structured use-after-close failure.
- The shared module contains no java.lang.foreign, Arrow Java, filesystem, ScalaFIM, or Gale types.
- Bench receipts cover scan, slice, validity traversal, and allocation behavior without unsupported zero-copy claims.
set.title: Frame foundation 1: Arrow-compatible batches and explicit ownership on JVM and JS
